turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth could not help but express her incredulity at Mr. Darcy’s claim of misfortunes, given his reputation and conduct.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: His pride wounded, Mr Darcy informed Elizabeth that his conduct had indeed been dictated by the most rigid adherence to proper principles.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth told Mr. Darcy that if his conduct had been guided by rigid principles, those principles must be flawed indeed, given his actions towards her family and Jane.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: His pride stung, Mr Darcy declared that his actions had been necessitated by the perceived impropriety and want of character in those around him.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth rolled her eyes at Mr Darcy’s self-righteous justification, telling him that such principles must be strangely constituted indeed to lead to such unjust and cruel actions towards others.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Mr Darcy retorted that his principles had been dictated by the necessity to preserve his family's honour and reputation, and he could not expect Elizabeth to comprehend such weighty responsibilities.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth was thoroughly unimpressed by Mr Darcy’s lofty justification, she told him, and such a narrow-minded sense of duty only served to alienate the very people one ought to honour and protect.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: He was clearly frustrated by her refusal to see reason, Darcy declared, his principles and actions were beyond reproach and his intentions towards Elizabeth’s family had been misconstrued.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Such a rigid sense of duty and honour, Elizabeth declared, only led to a life devoid of compassion and understanding.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: He was beyond exasperation with Elizabeth’s narrow-minded criticism, he declared, his intentions had always been above reproach and his actions dictated by the honour of his family.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Such rigid principles and actions, Elizabeth declared, only serve to isolate one from the very people one claims to protect and honour.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Such misguided principles, Elizabeth declared, only serve to perpetuate the very injustices Mr Darcy claims to abhor.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: He was at a loss for words, his pride clashing with the sincerity of his feelings, but finally he managed to convey his frustration and confusion to Elizabeth.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth was not swayed by Mr Darcy’s frustration, she told him, his actions spoke louder than his words and had caused too much pain to be easily forgiven.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: He was aware of his mistakes, he confessed to Elizabeth, and sought to mend the wrongs he had caused, however imperfect his efforts may seem.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth was unmoved by Mr Darcy’s confession, she told him, his past actions had done more harm than his present words could repair.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: He was conscious of the pain he had caused, Mr Darcy admitted, and vowed to make amends in ways that would prove his sincerity and commitment to change.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth was still unconvinced by Mr Darcy’s words, she told him, her heart was heavy with the memories of his past actions and the pain they had caused.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: He was acutely aware of the depth of Elizabeth’s pain and the weight of his past actions, yet he persisted, determined to prove his sincerity and commitment to change.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth was not convinced by Mr Darcy’s words, she told him, her heart was still burdened by the memories of his past actions and the pain they had caused.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy told Elizabeth that he had struggled in vain and that it would not do. His feelings would not be repressed, and he must allow him to tell her how ardently he admired and loved her.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth replied to Mr. Darcy that in such cases, it was believed to be the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. It was natural that obligation should be felt, and if she could feel gratitude, she would now thank him. But she could not, for she had never desired his good opinion, and he had certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. She was sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone, but it had been most unconsciously done and she hoped it would be of short duration. The feelings which he told her had long prevented the acknowledgment of his regard could have little difficulty in overcoming it after this explanation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy told Elizabeth that this was all the reply which he was to have the honour of expecting. He might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavour at civility, he was thus rejected. But it was of small importance.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth told Mr. Darcy that she might as well ask why, with such a clear intention of offending and insulting her, he chose to tell her that he liked her against his will, against his reason, and even against his character. Was not this some excuse for incivility, if she was uncivil? But she had other provocations. He knew she had. Had not her own feelings decided against him, had they been indifferent, or even favourable, did he think that any consideration would tempt her to accept the man who had been the means of ruining, perhaps forever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth told Mr. Darcy that she had every reason in the world to think ill of him. No motive could excuse the unjust and ungenerous part he had acted there. He dared not, he could not deny that he had been the principal, if not the only means of dividing them from each other, of exposing one to the censure of the world for caprice and instability, the other to its derision for disappointed hopes, and involving them both in misery of the acutest kind.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth told Mr. Darcy that it was not merely this affair on which her dislike was founded. Long before it had taken place, her opinion of him was decided. His character was unfolded in the recital which she had received many months ago from Mr. Wickham. On this subject, what could he have to say? In what imaginary act of friendship could he here defend himself? Or under what misrepresentation could he here impose upon others?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy told Elizabeth that she took an eager interest in that gentleman’s concerns.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth replied to Mr. Darcy that who that knew what his misfortunes had been could help feeling an interest in him?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy told Elizabeth that his misfortunes had indeed been great indeed.
